MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING ti THIS MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING is made and entered into this 27 , 2011, by and between the Metropolitan Office of Economic and ity Development (“ECD”) and the Metropolitan Department of Public Works WITNESSETH WHEREAS, pursuant to Executive Order No. 024, the ECD is responsible for the supervision of the Mayor’s Office of Film and Special Events (“FSE”); and WHEREAS, pursuant to Chapter 2.62 of the Metropolitan Code of Laws, FSE is charged with, among other things, coordinating with MPW regarding the closure and utilization of streets for film and special events; and WHEREAS, the FSE doesn’t have the administrative resources necessary to carry out all of its promulgated functions and could benefit by the administrative support of MPW; and WHEREAS, MPW has operational and personnel resources in place to issue permits, collect permit fees and and administer such processes; and WHEREAS, the parties have determined that the public interest will be best served and governmental resources used most efficiently by developing a closer connection between the personnel and operational activities associated with the issuance of permits and collection of permit fees and the personnel and operational activities of the Metropolitan Government relating to the administration and enforcement of such permits and fees; and WHEREAS, pursuant to the terms of this instrument, the parties have proposed that the public interest will best be served by placing the personnel and operational activities relating to FSE with MPW. NOW, THEREFORE, THE PARTIES AGREE AS FOLLOWS:
1. The term of this memorandum shall be indefinite. Either party may terminate this memorandum with written notice delivered to the director of the other department.
2. On and after July 29, 2011, all FSE personnel currently involved in activities relating to the issuance of FSE permits and collection of permit fees shall, together with their materials and equipment relating to such activities, transfer to offices under the administration of MPW.
3. After their transfer to MPW, the FSE personnel shall be subject to the supervision and direction of the MPW director or others he may designate.
4, After the effective date of this memorandum, FSE personnel, and any MPW administrative personnel that may be assigned to such work by the MPW director, shall carry out the responsibilities promulgated in Chapter 2.62 of the Metropolitan Code of Laws (“FSE Responsibilities”).
5. The MPW director shall keep separate accounting records pertaining to the FSE Responsibilities and shall provide copies of such records to the ECD director annually, or more frequently if the ECD director so requests, for review and approval.
6. Yearly on the anniversary of the effective date of this memorandum, the MPW director shall submit to the ECD director a detailed report of activities undertaken and funds expended in connection with the FSE Responsibilities during the preceding year.
7. Funds appropriated by the Metropolitan Council or otherwise made available for carrying out the FSE Responsibilities shall be assigned as necessary to MPW. The parties agree to execute such instruments as may be necessary to effect the provisions of this paragraph.
8. In the event this memorandum is terminated for any reason, the employees then involved in activities relating to the FSE Responsibilities shall, together with their materials and equipment relating to such activities, transfer to offices under the direct administration of ECD. 9, Nothing in this memorandum shall be construed as a limitation of the provisions of Chapter 2.62 of the Metropolitan Code of Laws. The parties shall cooperate in the development of procedures to assure that the FSE Responsibilities and other functions contemplated by the Metropolitan Code and Executive Orders are performed.
10. The parties recognize the likelihood that unanticipated problems may arise during the term of this memorandum and agree to work cooperatively to resolve such problems for the benefit of the Metropolitan Government.
11. The responsibilities established in this memorandum may not be assigned. Office of Economic and Community Metropolitan Department of Public Works Development . Matthew A. Wiltshire, Director W. Lynch, Director WA RECEIVED AUG -3 METROPOLITAN ARCHIVE
